dedupe_keys.name: forest roads of the congo basin sentinel based monthly road mapping wageningen university

description: This dataset maps the development of roads in the Congo Basin forest, monitored monthly from 2019 with a deep learning method applied to 10 m Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery for automated road detection. The Zenodo version gives four years of road development (35,944 km) from 2019 to 2022 as line features with attributes for the connected network identifier, segment length, network length and the month and year each segment opened. It was produced by Wageningen University & Research with The Nature Conservancy, the Canadian Forest Service and partners, as described in Slagter et al. (2024). Coverage is continental, the Congo Basin forest in Central Africa. The data are free under CC BY 4.0 and available to download as shapefile and GeoJSON; continuously updated maps can be viewed in a Google Earth Engine app and the collection is available in Earth Engine. Caveats: the roads are forest roads detected automatically from imagery, so detections depend on image conditions, and they carry no surface, condition or traffic attributes. The mapped roads support accessibility and exposure analyses in regions where official road data are sparse. They complement the Global Roads Inventory Project and are related to OpenStreetMap.
